title: If You Have Multiple Interests, Start A One-Person Business

sentences.en: I'm a very obsessive person because when I find something that I am interested in, truly interested in, nothing else matters.
sentences.zh: 我是一个非常痴迷的人，因为当我找到自己真正感兴趣的东西时，其他一切都不重要了。

sentences.en: My focus becomes seamless.
sentences.zh: 我的专注力变得毫无阻碍。

sentences.en: I could work 24 hours a day if I didn't value sleep.
sentences.zh: 如果我不在乎睡眠，我可以一天工作24小时。

sentences.en: It's all I think about.
sentences.zh: 我脑子里全是这件事。

sentences.en: It's all I learn about and it's all I want to do.
sentences.zh: 我学的全是这件事，我想做的也全是这件事。

sentences.en: And I've gone through these obsessive cycles multiple times in my life.
sentences.zh: 我人生中经历过很多次这种痴迷周期。

sentences.en: At first it was fitness, and then spirituality, and then digital art, photography, web development, then psychology and certain branches of philosophy and various high value skills that I was told to learn, like marketing, copywriting, sales.
sentences.zh: 一开始是健身，然后是灵性，然后是数字艺术、摄影、网页开发，然后是心理学和某些哲学分支，还有别人告诉我要学的各种高价值技能，比如营销、文案、销售。

sentences.en: ET cetera.
sentences.zh: 等等等等。

sentences.en: The things that are required to start a business, so to say.
sentences.zh: 也就是所谓创业所需的东西。

sentences.en: And personally, I know there are many people that have that quality as well.
sentences.zh: 就我个人而言，我知道很多人也有这种特质。

sentences.en: You're very obsessive.
sentences.zh: 你非常痴迷。

sentences.en: You love to learn, but when you look around you, there aren't too many people that also display that quality.
sentences.zh: 你热爱学习，但当你环顾四周，身边展现出这种特质的人并不多。

sentences.en: So I genuinely think that it's a superpower.
sentences.zh: 所以我真心认为这是一种超能力。

sentences.en: And I'm not just saying it because I have that quality, but I have noticed that it allows me to get very far ahead of other people very quickly, because for some reason, people just can't become interested in things.
sentences.zh: 我这么说不是因为我具备这种特质，而是我注意到它让我能非常迅速地远远领先于其他人，因为出于某种原因，人们就是无法对事物产生兴趣。

sentences.en: They don't find something interesting when if you look deep enough, everything is interesting, absolutely everything.
sentences.zh: 他们找不到有趣的东西，但如果你看得足够深，每件事都很有趣，绝对是每件事。

sentences.en: Just stare at your wall and then dig deeper.
sentences.zh: 就盯着你的墙看，然后往深处挖。

sentences.en: How was it built?
sentences.zh: 它是怎么建成的？

sentences.en: What is the process that went into making it?
sentences.zh: 建造它经历了什么过程？

sentences.en: Why is that outlet structured in that way?
sentences.zh: 那个插座为什么是那种结构？

sentences.en: So on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类。

sentences.en: You have an entire learning rabbit hole that you can go down with anything that you look at.
sentences.zh: 你看到的任何东西，都能让你进入一个完整的学习深坑。

sentences.en: So I don't really understand that.
sentences.zh: 所以我真的不太理解那种情况。

sentences.en: I'm not interested in anything.
sentences.zh: 我对什么都不感兴趣。

sentences.en: I think you're just distracted and you've engaged in so much pleasure seeking that simple things just don't bring you joy.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你只是分心了，你沉溺了太多追求快感的事情，以至于简单的事物已经无法给你带来快乐。

sentences.en: But if you do have multiple interests, there is a pretty big problem, and it's that society has convinced you that that trait or quality of loving learning or having multiple interests is a weakness.
sentences.zh: 但如果你确实有多重兴趣，有一个相当大的问题，那就是社会让你相信，热爱学习或拥有多重兴趣这种特质是一种弱点。

sentences.en: And you may even believe them because you spend your entire day learning or going down rabbit holes.
sentences.zh: 你甚至可能相信了他们，因为你整天都在学习或钻各种深坑。

sentences.en: And frankly, you don't really have much to show for it.
sentences.zh: 坦白说，你确实拿不出什么成果。

sentences.en: All you have is a bit of knowledge, and it's understandable why society, or just people in general think that.
sentences.zh: 你有的只是一点知识，而社会或普通人为什么这么想，是可以理解的。

sentences.en: Why they think that that trait is a weakness.
sentences.zh: 为什么他们认为那种特质是一种弱点。

sentences.en: It's because most people still have a worldview influenced by the industrial paradigm.
sentences.zh: 因为大多数人仍然持有一种被工业范式影响的世界观。

sentences.en: They fully believe that becoming a specialist, getting a job that requires you to perform a mechanical string of tasks for 40 years, and retiring at an age where your money can't be put to great use outside of buying material objects because you were deprived for so long, is still the best route to take in life.
sentences.zh: 他们完全相信，成为一个专才，找一份需要你机械地执行一串任务40年的工作，然后在一个你的钱除了买物质产品之外无法发挥更大用处的年纪退休——因为你被剥夺太久了——这仍然是人生最好的路径。

sentences.en: And I can confidently tell you that that is not the best route to take in life.
sentences.zh: 而我可以自信地告诉你，那不是人生最好的路径。

sentences.en: Therefore, having multiple interests is potentially a superpower.
sentences.zh: 因此，拥有多重兴趣很可能是一种超能力。

sentences.en: And that's why I'm creating these videos to show you why.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我在制作这些视频来告诉你原因。

sentences.en: First, it signals that you have high agency.
sentences.zh: 首先，这说明你有很强的自主性。

sentences.en: Second is signals that you have a unique point of view.
sentences.zh: 其次，这说明你有独特的视角。

sentences.en: And three, it signals that you have everything required to turn your interests into a modern source of income, because that's every person's dream.
sentences.zh: 第三，这说明你具备把兴趣转化为现代收入来源所需的一切，因为这是每个人的梦想。

sentences.en: If you have multiple interests, you want to be able to pursue those things full time.
sentences.zh: 如果你有多种兴趣，你希望能全职去追求这些事。

sentences.en: And there are many ways to do that in today's world.
sentences.zh: 在今天这个世界，有很多方式可以做到。

sentences.en: But I want to show you one way that is just a logical way of doing it.
sentences.zh: 但我想给你看一种方式，一种符合逻辑的做法。

sentences.en: It is probably the best way of doing it.
sentences.zh: 这可能是最好的方式。

sentences.en: So in this video, I want to break it all down.
sentences.zh: 所以在这个视频里，我想把这一切拆解清楚。

sentences.en: I want to break down why people who learn quickly and have multiple interests are already ahead of most of the population.
sentences.zh: 我想拆解为什么那些学得快、有多种兴趣的人，已经领先了大多数人。

sentences.en: I want to break down how you already do 80% of the work required to make an income.
sentences.zh: 我想拆解你是如何已经完成了赚钱所需的 80% 的工作。

sentences.en: That is, you already research.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，你已经在做研究了。

sentences.en: You just don't think of it as that.
sentences.zh: 只是你没把它当成研究。

sentences.en: And then I want to break down your options to start earning a side or full time income, preferably by discovering and pursuing your life's work.
sentences.zh: 然后我想拆解你的选项，如何开始赚取副业或全职收入，最好是通过发现并追求你一生的事业。

sentences.en: Yes, that's a bit deep.
sentences.zh: 没错，这有点深。

sentences.en: You're probably just here to make money, but trust me, it's a lot better if it's meaningful money.
sentences.zh: 你可能只是来学怎么赚钱的，但相信我，如果是有意义的钱，那会好得多。

sentences.en: So with all of that, let's begin.
sentences.zh: 好，说了这么多，我们开始吧。

sentences.en: And for part one, I want to talk about why learners and improvers.
sentences.zh: 第一部分，我想聊聊为什么学习者和自我提升者。

sentences.en: So like self improvers have more leverage than ever before.
sentences.zh: 也就是那些自我提升者，比以往任何时候都拥有更多杠杆。

sentences.en: And we'll start with a quote from naval code.
sentences.zh: 我们先引用 Naval 的一句话。

sentences.en: And media are permissionless leverage their the leverage behind the newly rich.
sentences.zh: 媒体是无须许可的杠杆，是新富阶层背后的杠杆。

sentences.en: You can create software and media that works for you while you sleep.
sentences.zh: 你可以创造软件和媒体，在你睡觉时为你工作。

sentences.en: So for many people you hear code and that doesn't really ring a bell for you, right?
sentences.zh: 对很多人来说，听到代码这个词，你可能没什么感觉，对吧？

sentences.en: You're not a programmer, you're not a coder.
sentences.zh: 你不是程序员，不会写代码。

sentences.en: And media may not ring a bell for you either, because like, what does that mean?
sentences.zh: 媒体这个词你可能也没什么感觉，因为，这到底是什么意思？

sentences.en: In today's world, that means content.
sentences.zh: 在今天的世界，它指的就是内容。

sentences.en: In the past, it meant the radio, maybe billboards, maybe books, maybe physical mail, maybe the newspaper. But today it's content.
sentences.zh: 在过去，它指的是广播，也许是广告牌，也许是书，也许是实体邮件，也许是报纸。但今天，它就是内容。

sentences.en: And what you may not understand is that, yes, content can work for you while you sleep.
sentences.zh: 你可能没意识到的是，没错，内容可以在你睡觉时为你工作。

sentences.en: This YouTube video probably has a link to it in my software that some people will pay for, and this YouTube video will continue growing over time and driving traffic to that offer.
sentences.zh: 这个 YouTube 视频在我的软件里可能有一个链接，有些人会为此付费，而这个 YouTube 视频会随着时间持续增长，把流量导向那个产品。

sentences.en: So two things a source of traffic media.
sentences.zh: 所以两样东西：流量来源，也就是媒体。

sentences.en: This video creating it on a consistent schedule and having a strategy and to your offer what you're selling that allows you to not sell an offer or a product for the boss that you're working for so that you can do it independently.
sentences.zh: 这个视频，按固定节奏持续创作，加上一套策略，再加上你的产品，也就是你在卖的东西，这让你不必再为你老板卖产品或服务，你可以独立去做。

sentences.en: Oh, I don't want to sell an offer.
sentences.zh: 哦，我不想卖产品。

sentences.en: You're already selling one.
sentences.zh: 你已经在卖了。

sentences.en: You're playing the role that your boss gave you to sell the product that they're selling.
sentences.zh: 你在扮演你老板给你的角色，去卖他们在卖的产品。

sentences.en: So all you need to do is sell a product that you actually want to sell, and then create media to sell it.
sentences.zh: 所以你只需要去卖一个你真正想卖的产品，然后创作媒体来卖它。

sentences.en: But there's a lot that goes into that, right?
sentences.zh: 但这里面有很多门道，对吧？

sentences.en: That's why we're here.
sentences.zh: 所以我们才会在这里。

sentences.en: So you as an individual have more leverage than ever before.
sentences.zh: 你作为一个个体，现在拥有的杠杆比以往任何时候都大。

sentences.en: Leverage in this context is the multiplier between input and output.
sentences.zh: 在这个语境下，杠杆就是输入和输出之间的乘数。

sentences.en: In other words, a small action can create a disproportionately large effect, and technology continues to increase the power in individual holds. Because just think about it.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，一个微小的行动可以产生不成比例的巨大效果，而技术还在持续增强个体手中的力量。你想想看。

sentences.en: When social media became a thing, or even the internet became a thing, you can now write an article, or a social media post, or a tweet, or real that has the potential to reach millions of people.
sentences.zh: 当社交媒体出现，甚至互联网出现的时候，你现在可以写一篇文章、一条社交媒体帖子、一条推文或者一个 Reel，它就有可能触达数百万人。

sentences.en: That was impossible with the radio.
sentences.zh: 这在广播时代是不可能的。

sentences.en: You probably will never get on the radio or television.
sentences.zh: 你大概永远上不了广播或电视。

sentences.en: And imagine in the past, imagine trying to send a million handwritten letters to people around the world.
sentences.zh: 再想象一下过去，想象一下试图给全世界的人手写寄出一百万封信。

sentences.en: It just doesn't work that way.
sentences.zh: 根本行不通。

sentences.en: So what this means is that the average, everyday person now has the potential to reach a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 所以这意味着，普通的、日常的个体，现在有了触达大量人群的潜力。

sentences.en: Maybe not millions, but even thousands is crazy.
sentences.zh: 也许不是几百万人，但哪怕几千人也已经很疯狂了。

sentences.en: What if one person, what if a thousand people pay you a certain amount of money per month?
sentences.zh: 如果一个人——如果一千个人每个月付你一笔钱呢？

sentences.en: You're set.
sentences.zh: 你就稳了。

sentences.en: You're not a mega millionaire because you don't have to be, but you've effectively replaced your salary and probably then some more.
sentences.zh: 你不是超级百万富翁，因为你不需要是，但你已经有效地替代了你的薪水，而且可能还多出不少。

sentences.en: And now this is still possible.
sentences.zh: 而这件事现在仍然可能。

sentences.en: Social media has evolved and the market has become sophisticated.
sentences.zh: 社交媒体已经进化了，市场也变得成熟了。

sentences.en: But that doesn't mean that you can't learn that you're a learner.
sentences.zh: 但这不代表你不能学，你是一个学习者。

sentences.en: That's why I'm saying this is a superpower is because you can acquire the skill and you can create the strategy through dedicated learning and research that allows you to do this, because most people won't do that.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我说这是一种超能力，因为你可以通过专注的学习和研究，去获取这项技能、去制定这套策略，让你做到这件事，因为大多数人不会这么做。

sentences.en: And the thing about understanding is that people create excuses for things that they don't understand.
sentences.zh: 而关于理解这件事，有一点是：人们会为自己不理解的东西制造借口。

sentences.en: And if excuses are for the incompetent, then incompetent people will think, oh, social media is just about luck.
sentences.zh: 如果借口是属于无能者的，那么无能的人就会想：哦，社交媒体就是靠运气。

sentences.en: Everyone's posting content, but only a few get picked to do well, when in reality, the ones that get picked to do well are the people who treat it as their full time job to study and understand why that mechanism works.
sentences.zh: 所有人都在发内容，但只有少数人被选中做得好，而实际上，那些被选中做得好的人，是把这件事当成全职工作去研究、去理解那个机制为什么有效的人。

sentences.en: You just see it as people posting on social media because you're a consumer.
sentences.zh: 你只是把它看成人们在社交媒体上发东西，因为你是一个消费者。

sentences.en: You're not the person doing it, you're not in the game.
sentences.zh: 你不是那个在做这件事的人，你不在游戏里。

sentences.en: You haven't studied that domain of knowledge.
sentences.zh: 你没有研究过那个知识领域。

sentences.en: And yes, it's a domain of knowledge.
sentences.zh: 是的，它是一个知识领域。

sentences.en: Like anything else, you don't understand it.
sentences.zh: 跟其他任何东西一样，你不理解它。

sentences.en: So you label it as this simple little thing that your mind can understand.
sentences.zh: 所以你就把它标签化，当成一个你的大脑能够理解的简单小东西。

sentences.en: And then you look at that simple little thing and you think, oh, that's useless, or oh, I can't do this.
sentences.zh: 然后你看着那个简单小东西，你想：哦，那没用，或者，哦，我做不到这个。

sentences.en: But the other thing here related to leverage is that now AI has become a thing, and the ability to code or program another form of leverage has become democratized so that most people can do it.
sentences.zh: 但跟杠杆相关的另一件事是，现在 AI 已经出现了，编程能力——另一种形式的杠杆——已经被民主化了，以至于大多数人都能做到。

sentences.en: Are you going to build the next notion or the next Salesforce or the next whatever, big software, the next social media platform?
sentences.zh: 你会去构建下一个 Notion，或者下一个 Salesforce，或者下一个什么大型软件、下一个社交媒体平台吗？

sentences.en: No, probably not, unless you have an entire dev team behind you.
sentences.zh: 不会，大概不会，除非你背后有一整支开发团队。

sentences.en: But most average people can absolutely build a small scale digital product that they can sell, accompanied by a full marketing funnel that they can have the AI build out.
sentences.zh: 但大多数普通人绝对可以构建一个小规模的数字产品来卖，再配上一整套 AI 可以帮你搭建出来的完整营销漏斗。

sentences.en: And does that mean that everything is written by AI?
sentences.zh: 而这是否意味着所有东西都由 AI 来写？

sentences.en: No. You have to impress your personal taste on it so that it sounds like you.
sentences.zh: 不是。你得把自己的品味烙印在上面，让它听起来像你。

sentences.en: And so that actually works.
sentences.zh: 这样才真的有用。

sentences.en: But building the thing or building the prototype of the thing has become faster than ever.
sentences.zh: 但构建产品、或者构建产品原型，比以往任何时候都快了。

sentences.en: So in other words, you can do the thing that used to take a team of ten, 20, 30, 40, 50 people as one person.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，你一个人就能做到过去需要十人、二十人、三十人、四十人、五十人团队才能做的事。

sentences.en: Now, this was always possible with something like social media and information products.
sentences.zh: 其实，这在社交媒体和信息产品这类事情上，一直都是可能的。

sentences.en: That was what my old one person business videos talked about, where you pretty much build a social media audience.
sentences.zh: 那是我以前那些一人企业视频讲的内容：你基本上就是建立一个社交媒体受众。

sentences.en: You write content for two hours a day, and then you create a digital product and you sell that product in your content.
sentences.zh: 每天写两小时内容，然后做一个数字产品，在你的内容里卖那个产品。

sentences.en: But information products are abundant.
sentences.zh: 但信息产品已经泛滥了。

sentences.en: Anyone can create them.
sentences.zh: 谁都能做。

sentences.en: I don't think they're going to die, but we're going to talk about all of that now, to start to ground this so that you can understand it as a person with multiple interests, or a person who just has one interest and wants to share it or wants to turn it into a business.
sentences.zh: 我不觉得它们会消亡，但我们现在要聊聊这一切，先打好基础，让你作为一个有多种兴趣的人——或者只有一种兴趣、想分享它、想把它变成生意的人——能够理解。

sentences.en: Paul Mousseau is a great example.
sentences.zh: Paul Mousseau 是个很好的例子。

sentences.en: He has built a modern philosophy school on Substack.
sentences.zh: 他在 Substack 上建了一所现代哲学学校。

sentences.en: He quite literally just teaches philosophy on Substack.
sentences.zh: 他真的就是在 Substack 上教哲学。

sentences.en: That's the paid tier of his Substack.
sentences.zh: 那是他 Substack 的付费层级。

sentences.en: He does weekly lectures that people can attend.
sentences.zh: 他每周做讲座，人们可以参加。

sentences.en: And now I've talked about this in my book.
sentences.zh: 我在我的书里也讲过这个。

sentences.en: It's free on my Substack called Purpose and Profit, but I see the good parts of the creator economy as somewhat of a decentralized education system.
sentences.zh: 这本书在我的 Substack 上免费，叫《Purpose and Profit》，但我把创作者经济里好的那部分，看作某种去中心化的教育系统。

sentences.en: Passionate individuals dive deep into their interests, pull out the compelling parts, make them useful, and teach them.
sentences.zh: 充满热情的人深入钻研自己的兴趣，提炼出最引人入胜的部分，让它们变得有用，然后教给别人。

sentences.en: Most people these days get most of their education related to their goals, not their parents goals, not their universities goals.
sentences.zh: 如今大多数人获取的、跟自己目标相关的教育——不是父母的目标，不是大学的目标——大部分都来自 YouTube 和社交媒体，来自那些跟他们产生共鸣的创作者。

sentences.en: From places like YouTube and social media, from the creators they resonate with.
sentences.zh: 来自 YouTube 和社交媒体，来自那些跟他们产生共鸣的创作者。

sentences.en: You're probably not learning about what I'm sharing in this video in college.
sentences.zh: 你大概不会在大学里学到我这支视频分享的东西。

sentences.en: In high school, you're not.
sentences.zh: 在高中，你更学不到。

sentences.en: You have to supplement.
sentences.zh: 你必须自己补充。

sentences.en: You have to self educate with people who are sharing what you want to learn on YouTube or other social media platforms, and their entire business model.
sentences.zh: 你必须跟那些在 YouTube 或其他社交媒体平台上分享你想学的东西的人自我教育，而他们的整个商业模式——

sentences.en: My entire business model is improve yourself and then improve others.
sentences.zh: 我的整个商业模式就是：先提升自己，再提升别人。

sentences.en: In other words, if you have interests to talk about, you have a way of building an audience.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，如果你有想聊的兴趣，你就有一条建立受众的路。

sentences.en: You have traffic, you have leverage.
sentences.zh: 你就有流量，你就有杠杆。

sentences.en: The difficulty lies in talking about your interests in a way that captures attention and makes people want to follow you.
sentences.zh: 难点在于，如何用一种能抓住注意力、让人想关注你的方式去聊你的兴趣。

sentences.en: And this is exactly why I built Eden, because it makes it nearly impossible to not generate ideas worth writing about, and then it guides you through actually writing them.
sentences.zh: 这正是我打造 Eden 的原因，因为它让你几乎不可能想不出值得写的点子，然后它还会引导你真正把它们写出来。

sentences.en: It's your AI content strategist, so to say.
sentences.zh: 可以说，它就是你的 AI 内容策略师。

sentences.en: At least that's what we're building it to be.
sentences.zh: 至少我们正在把它打造成这样。

sentences.en: It researches what's popular in your niche or in the interest that you talk about, and then it understands who you are, your voice and your own content.
sentences.zh: 它会研究你的细分领域或你聊的兴趣里什么内容受欢迎，然后它会理解你是谁、你的声音和你自己的内容。

sentences.en: If you're already a creator and then it synthesizes the two.
sentences.zh: 如果你已经是一个创作者，然后它会把这两者合成。

sentences.en: So it takes what's already good, it takes what is good from you or has potential, and then it gives you daily ideas that you can take, make your own and run with.
sentences.zh: 所以它提取已经很好的东西，提取你身上好的、或者有潜力的东西，然后给你每天的点子，你可以拿去，变成你自己的，然后放手去干。

sentences.en: And it's also an outlier tool.
sentences.zh: 而且它也是一个 outlier 工具。

sentences.en: So any of the tools you would use to find good ideas on social media or to research social media, this is what content strategists for big YouTubers or big social media accounts use.
sentences.zh: 你在社交媒体上找好点子、或者做社交媒体调研会用到的任何工具，本来就是那些大 YouTuber 或大号的内容策略师在用的。

sentences.en: Then you can just use Eden instead.
sentences.zh: 那你直接用 Eden 就行了。

sentences.en: We're actually working with a few big creators right now to build features that they would benefit from, so their content teams are able to actually use this more than they're already able to, and they're getting quite good results out of it.
sentences.zh: 我们现在其实正在跟几个大创作者合作，开发一些对他们有用的功能，这样他们的内容团队就能比现在用得更好，而且他们已经拿到了相当不错的结果。

sentences.en: We had someone the other day reach out saying that they used to eat an AI chat and their next two posts, so the idea is that they got from Eden that were arguably their own in their own voice, got 3 million views apiece, and they posted those two posts on the same day.
sentences.zh: 前几天有人联系我们，说他们以前用 AI 聊天来写接下来两篇帖子，而他们从 Eden 拿到的点子——基本上是他们自己的、用自己的声音写出来的——每篇都拿到了 300 万播放，而且这两篇是同一天发的。

sentences.en: That is absurd.
sentences.zh: 这太离谱了。

sentences.en: So if you want 50% off your first month, you can sign up, link in the description, and then after that, you now have a way of understanding and reverse engineering how to package up your interest so that they get attention, which we'll talk more about.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你想首月打五折，可以点描述里的链接注册，之后你就有了一个方法，去理解并逆向拆解怎么把你的兴趣包装起来、让它们获得注意力，这个我们后面会细讲。

sentences.en: But if you understand how to package that up or turn that into a product that people will pay you for, then you have a way of monetizing your interest.
sentences.zh: 但如果你懂得怎么把它包装起来，或者把它变成一个人们愿意付费的产品，那你就有了一个把兴趣变现的方法。

sentences.en: You have a business, and if you don't like the word business, then just think of it as getting paid for what you do.
sentences.zh: 你就有了一门生意，如果你不喜欢"生意"这个词，那就把它想成：你做的东西能赚钱。

sentences.en: That's what a business is.
sentences.zh: 生意就是这个。

sentences.en: Don't overcomplicate it.
sentences.zh: 别把它搞复杂了。

sentences.en: Don't assign any negative connotation to the word business because you think it's not for you.
sentences.zh: 别因为你觉得自己不是那块料，就给"生意"这个词贴上负面标签。

sentences.en: So now, part two, I want to talk about how to turn your love for learning into a business.
sentences.zh: 好，现在第二部分，我想聊聊怎么把你对学习的热爱变成一门生意。

sentences.en: And in this part we're going to break down what your brand, content and product should actually look like.
sentences.zh: 这部分我们要拆解你的品牌、内容和产品到底应该长什么样。

sentences.en: So to the point of what this business model is and how to turn multiple interests into a business, you teach your interests.
sentences.zh: 回到这个商业模式是什么、以及怎么把多重兴趣变成一门生意的问题上：你教你的兴趣。

sentences.en: That's what you do.
sentences.zh: 这就是你要做的事。

sentences.en: You teach, or you turn what you would have taught into an implementation tool.
sentences.zh: 你去教，或者把你本来要教的东西变成一个落地工具。

sentences.en: And we'll talk about that because that's a bit more modern, that's a bit more you dive into the vibe coding or programing aspect of things, even though I don't really care for the word vibe coding, because I feel like that's carrying a negative connotation, and it makes people believe that if they vibe code, they're doing something cheap.
sentences.zh: 这个我们会聊到，因为这更现代一点，更偏向你去接触 vibe coding 或者编程相关的东西，虽然我不太喜欢 vibe coding 这个词，因为我觉得它带着负面含义，让人觉得如果 vibe coding，就是在做廉价的东西。

sentences.en: But in reality, the people that are vibe coding that also have the knowledge of marketing and sales are doing a lot better than the programmers who don't have the marketing and sales knowledge, because the people with the marketing and sales knowledge are able to create a much better product.
sentences.zh: 但现实是，那些既会 vibe coding 又懂营销和销售的人，比那些不懂营销和销售的程序员做得好得多，因为懂营销和销售的人能做出好得多的产品。

sentences.en: Is it perfectly written code? No. Do I think that's a requirement to a good product?
sentences.zh: 代码写得完美吗？不。但我觉得那是好产品的必要条件吗？

sentences.en: Probably not, especially in the future.
sentences.zh: 大概率不是，尤其是在未来。

sentences.en: And other people think that vibe coding or getting into or just like building some kind of tool with AI is just too easier. It's too cheap.
sentences.zh: 还有人觉得 vibe coding、或者用 AI 搞个什么工具，太简单了，太廉价了。

sentences.en: They think of it as like, honestly, they think of it as a tier lower than info products, because info products actually require you to have knowledge and other things like that.
sentences.zh: 说实话，他们觉得这比信息产品还低一档，因为信息产品至少需要你有知识什么的。

sentences.en: But again, we'll talk about that now for a little story that I feel like a lot of you can resonate with.
sentences.zh: 不过这个我们待会再聊，先讲一个小故事，我觉得很多人会有共鸣。

sentences.en: The other day I was outside working at a coffee shop with my buddies, as I do quite often, and I had someone who noticed me from YouTube, which was pretty cool, and eventually they asked for advice on what they should monetize, and they said that they were trying to do videographers for real estate personal brands, and they had some clients doing that, and he said that he could scale it.
sentences.zh: 前几天我在外面跟朋友们在咖啡店工作，我经常这样，有个人从 YouTube 认出了我，挺酷的，后来他们问我该变现什么，他们说自己在尝试给房地产个人品牌做视频拍摄，已经有了一些客户，还说这个可以规模化。

sentences.en: But he said in an ideal world, he wanted to do something more artistic and creative. Right?
sentences.zh: 但他说，在理想世界里，他想做更艺术、更有创意的东西。对吧？

sentences.en: He wanted to do the filmmaking aspect of things.
sentences.zh: 他想做电影感的那一面。

sentences.en: And so I asked, is he creating content for his own brand?
sentences.zh: 于是我问，他有在为自己的品牌创作内容吗？

sentences.en: He said no. And to me it was kind of obvious.
sentences.zh: 他说没有。对我来说这其实挺明显的。

sentences.en: He should express the artistic side by using filmmaking and videography in his own videos to make them nice, beautiful, and have them stand out.
sentences.zh: 他应该把艺术那一面表达出来，用电影感和视频拍摄技巧来做他自己的视频，把它们做得好看、漂亮、能脱颖而出。

sentences.en: That's a part of his unique edge.
sentences.zh: 这是他独特优势的一部分。

sentences.en: And then he should teach what he's passionate about videography and filmmaking.
sentences.zh: 然后他应该去教他热爱的视频拍摄和电影感创作。

sentences.en: Two personal brands which he already has some experience in, and that's like a glaring gap in the market, is a lot of personal brands just don't know how to edit.
sentences.zh: 教给个人品牌，这个领域他已经有一些经验了，而这就是市场上一个明显的缺口：很多个人品牌就是不知道怎么剪辑。

sentences.en: There isn't a day that goes by where I don't get an email, where it's like people are thinking too hard, or think that recording video is like a very high barrier of entry because they don't know what editing tool to use or they don't want to learn it, or so on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 没有一天我不收到邮件，说人们想太多，或者觉得录视频门槛很高，因为他们不知道用什么剪辑工具、或者不想学，等等等等。

sentences.en: So not only would this attract videography and filmmaking clients for him by posting his own content, because he's now positioning himself as an authority by teaching other people what he has learned, but he would also build a broad enough audience so that he could eventually create a product that can sell without him actually fulfilling a service so he can sell while he sleeps.
sentences.zh: 这样一来，他不仅可以通过发布自己的内容来吸引摄像和电影制作的客户——因为他现在通过教别人自己学到的东西，把自己定位成了权威——而且他还能建立一个足够广泛的受众群，最终创造出一个不需要他实际提供服务就能销售的产品，让他在睡觉时也能赚钱。

sentences.en: And he could just create something that teaches or helps personal brands or other people get into videography or filmmaking.
sentences.zh: 他只需要创造一些东西，来教个人品牌或其他想入行的人如何做摄像或电影制作。

sentences.en: And the main question here is like, okay, well, what if I don't consider myself an expert?
sentences.zh: 这里的主要问题是，好吧，如果我不认为自己是专家怎么办？

sentences.en: What if I don't have experience in something like videography or filmmaking and don't feel comfortable enough teaching it?
sentences.zh: 如果我没有摄像或电影制作这类经验，教起来心里没底怎么办？

sentences.en: That's why you position yourself as a student and a researcher rather than an expert.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么你要把自己定位成一个学生和研究者，而不是专家。

sentences.en: You don't have to claim results.
sentences.zh: 你不需要宣称自己有什么成果。

sentences.en: You don't have to claim that your videography skills are going to ten x their views overnight.
sentences.zh: 你不需要宣称你的摄像技巧能让他们一夜之间观看量翻十倍。

sentences.en: Learning the skill in and of itself if the tip is useful, is useful.
sentences.zh: 学习这个技能本身，只要技巧有用，就是有价值的。

sentences.en: And so that's only one example, but I feel like the same applies to you.
sentences.zh: 这只是一个例子，但我觉得同样的逻辑也适用于你。

sentences.en: You don't have a lot of capital to invest, so certain business models are off the table.
sentences.zh: 你没有太多资金可以投入，所以某些商业模式对你来说行不通。

sentences.en: You don't care to fundraise, and you kind of just want to do something creative and meaningful.
sentences.zh: 你不想去融资，你只是想做一些有创造性、有意义的事情。

sentences.en: And so for people who have a love for learning, here's kind of the gist of what a business would look like for you.
sentences.zh: 所以对于那些热爱学习的人来说，你的生意大概会是这个样子。

sentences.en: First, you study your interests.
sentences.zh: 首先，研究你的兴趣。

sentences.en: That's the first thing.
sentences.zh: 这是第一件事。

sentences.en: They are inherently valuable because you value them, meaning someone else can value them too.
sentences.zh: 它们天然就有价值，因为你重视它们，这意味着别人也可能重视它们。

sentences.en: And many already value them and know people can't just ask AI because they often don't know what to ask.
sentences.zh: 而且很多人已经重视它们了，他们没法直接问AI，因为他们往往不知道该问什么。

sentences.en: Second is you learn how to package them because you aren't Marcus Aurelius.
sentences.zh: 第二，学会如何包装它们，因为你又不是马可·奥勒留。

sentences.en: Writing fortune cookie tweets isn't going to get you anywhere.
sentences.zh: 写一些鸡汤金句推文不会让你有任何进展。

sentences.en: You must understand attention, mechanics and engagement psychology.
sentences.zh: 你必须理解注意力机制和参与心理学。

sentences.en: And now that you know what to ask, AI research that.
sentences.zh: 现在你知道该问什么了，用AI去研究这些。

sentences.en: Third, you weave in your unique voice because your audience doesn't care if you have new ideas.
sentences.zh: 第三，融入你独特的声音，因为你的受众不在乎你有没有新想法。

sentences.en: They want your opinion, your point of view on an idea that works.
sentences.zh: 他们想要的是你对一个有效想法的看法、你的观点。

sentences.en: And if you don't know what your voice is, build it.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不知道自己的声音是什么，去构建它。

sentences.en: In Eden, we have a feature called identities that will just guide you through a conversation and extract your unique voice or identity out of you, and then apply it whenever you're chatting with ideas.
sentences.zh: 在Eden里，我们有一个叫"身份"的功能，它会通过对话引导你，提取出你独特的声音或身份，然后在你和想法对话时自动应用它。

sentences.en: And fourth, you turn yourself into the business.
sentences.zh: 第四，把自己变成这个生意本身。

sentences.en: Your brand, content, and product all stem from your interests in the transformation they can provide.
sentences.zh: 你的品牌、内容和产品，都源于你的兴趣以及它们能带来的转变。

sentences.en: So your soul job is to become a researcher and a vessel.
sentences.zh: 所以你唯一的任务，就是成为一个研究者和一个载体。

sentences.en: And I'm serious about this.
sentences.zh: 我是认真的。

sentences.en: You must consider it to your full time job to research.
sentences.zh: 你必须把研究当成你的全职工作。

sentences.en: You need to be reading books.
sentences.zh: 你需要读书。

sentences.en: You need to be watching YouTube videos.
sentences.zh: 你需要看YouTube视频。

sentences.en: You need to be listening to podcasts.
sentences.zh: 你需要听播客。

sentences.en: You need to be looking at the discover tab in Eden because that's what writers, creatives and visionaries do.
sentences.zh: 你需要去看Eden里的发现页面，因为那是写作者、创造者和远见者做的事。

sentences.en: That's what Jordan Peterson does.
sentences.zh: 那是Jordan Peterson做的事。

sentences.en: That's what Andrew Huberman does.
sentences.zh: Andrew Huberman 也是这样做的。

sentences.en: That's what Marcus Aurelius and all your beloved figureheads of the past did.
sentences.zh: Marcus Aurelius 和你崇拜的所有历史人物都是这样做的。

sentences.en: They probably don't care about being a quote unquote personal brand, but they do care about their interests.
sentences.zh: 他们可能根本不在乎自己是不是所谓的"个人品牌"，但他们在乎自己的兴趣。

sentences.en: So creating content, which was once just considered writing before it took the specific form of media on the internet, is their chosen vessel for earning an income.
sentences.zh: 所以创作内容——在互联网上以特定媒体形式出现之前，它曾经就只是写作——是他们选择的谋生载体。

sentences.en: They read weird books.
sentences.zh: 他们读奇怪的书。

sentences.en: They find themselves in esoteric rabbit holes on the internet.
sentences.zh: 他们在互联网上钻进各种冷门的兔子洞。

sentences.en: They curate idea sources they love and save them in a safe place.
sentences.zh: 他们精心收集自己热爱的想法来源，把它们保存在一个安全的地方。

sentences.en: They question what most people think, gather multiple perspectives, and synthesize a unique one.
sentences.zh: 他们质疑大多数人的想法，收集多种视角，然后合成一个独特的观点。

sentences.en: They jot down thoughts like mad scientists.
sentences.zh: 他们像疯狂的科学家一样随手记下想法。

sentences.en: They are all ideal workers.
sentences.zh: 他们都是理想的工作者。

sentences.en: They hunt for ideas and share the best ones.
sentences.zh: 他们猎取想法，然后分享最好的那些。

sentences.en: Because 80% of writing comes from research, the other 20% is structuring and writing it the way that only you could.
sentences.zh: 因为写作的 80% 来自研究，另外 20% 是用只有你才能做到的方式去组织和表达。

sentences.en: So the question then is how do you actually build a tangible brand, content and product?
sentences.zh: 那么问题来了：你到底怎么建立一个有形的品牌、内容和产品？

sentences.en: So starting with brand, your brand is the transformation.
sentences.zh: 先从品牌说起，你的品牌就是转变。

sentences.en: Remember that that's your guiding light.
sentences.zh: 记住，这是你的指路明灯。

sentences.en: Brand is transformation.
sentences.zh: 品牌就是转变。

sentences.en: Because when you think of a person that you admire, why do you admire them?
sentences.zh: 因为当你想到一个你钦佩的人，你为什么钦佩他？

sentences.en: It's because they have changed your life in some fundamental way.
sentences.zh: 是因为他在某个根本层面上改变了你的人生。

sentences.en: Their content or product led to behavior change.
sentences.zh: 他的内容或产品带来了行为改变。

sentences.en: They first changed your mind, and then they changed your actions.
sentences.zh: 他先改变了你的想法，然后改变了你的行动。

sentences.en: And then the results that came from those actions you associated with that person.
sentences.zh: 而你把那些行动带来的结果，和那个人关联在一起。

sentences.en: You gave them credit for it.
sentences.zh: 你把功劳归于他。

sentences.en: James clear as an example, convince millions of people to adopt tiny habits that went on to make big changes.
sentences.zh: 以 James Clear 为例，他说服了数百万人养成微小习惯，这些习惯最终带来了巨大改变。

sentences.en: Jordan Peterson, in his prime, convinced millions of young men to take responsibility for their lives and pursue meaning.
sentences.zh: Jordan Peterson 在他的巅峰时期，说服了数百万年轻男性为自己的人生承担责任，去追寻意义。

sentences.en: Alan Watts help people stop taking life so seriously.
sentences.zh: Alan Watts 帮助人们不再把人生看得那么沉重。

sentences.en: Naval Ravikant taught people the power of digital leverage.
sentences.zh: Naval Ravikant 教会了人们数字杠杆的力量。

sentences.en: So if you heard an idea from navel and then you notice the outcome of that idea in your life, you would attribute that outcome to navel.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你从 Naval 那里听到一个想法，然后你在自己的人生中看到了这个想法带来的结果，你就会把那个结果归功于 Naval。

sentences.en: So your brand as a person with multiple interest is how you help people change their lives with those interests.
sentences.zh: 所以作为一个拥有多种兴趣的人，你的品牌就是你如何用这些兴趣帮助人们改变人生。

sentences.en: The more people you help, the stronger your brand becomes.
sentences.zh: 你帮助的人越多，你的品牌就越强。

sentences.en: And now people get stuck on their brand all the time.
sentences.zh: 现在，人们总是在品牌这件事上卡住。

sentences.en: They think they need the perfect bio or tagline or value proposition.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得自己需要一个完美的简介、标语或价值主张。

sentences.en: And in reality, you don't really need to say any of those things.
sentences.zh: 而实际上，你根本不需要说这些东西。

sentences.en: If you go to some of the profiles or creators that you really like, they usually don't have a bio.
sentences.zh: 如果你去看看你真正喜欢的一些创作者的主页，他们通常没有简介。

sentences.en: They don't have anything there, or at least anything of substance.
sentences.zh: 那里什么都没有，或者至少没有任何实质性的东西。

sentences.en: And that's the thing.
sentences.zh: 这就是关键所在。

sentences.en: People read your bio maybe once or twice when they visit your profile, and sometimes it's not even the guiding factor as to whether or not they're going to follow you.
sentences.zh: 别人访问你主页的时候，你的简介他们可能只看一两次，有时候那甚至不是他们决定关不关注你的主导因素。

sentences.en: Your brand is invisible.
sentences.zh: 你的品牌是无形的。

sentences.en: It's an image in people's minds that accumulates as they read your content, buy your products, change their behavior, and tell other people about you.
sentences.zh: 它是人们脑海中累积起来的一个形象，随着他们读你的内容、买你的产品、改变自己的行为、向别人提起你，这个形象就慢慢形成了。

sentences.en: So all you really need to do is answer three questions and have them guide most of your content, because your content will create your brand.
sentences.zh: 所以你真正需要做的，就是回答三个问题，让它们来引导你大部分的内容，因为你的内容会塑造你的品牌。

sentences.en: So the first question is who can you help the most and what does their life look like now?
sentences.zh: 第一个问题是：你能帮到最多的人是谁，他们现在的生活是什么样子？

sentences.en: Question two is what has changed your life the most?
sentences.zh: 第二个问题是：什么改变了你的人生最多？

sentences.en: So what interests do you see as important?
sentences.zh: 也就是，你认为哪些兴趣是重要的？

sentences.en: Question three is how can you help other people do the same?
sentences.zh: 第三个问题是：你怎么帮别人做到同样的事？

sentences.en: So what about their mind and actions need to change and how can you help them change?
sentences.zh: 他们的思维和行动需要发生什么改变，你又怎么帮他们实现这种改变？

sentences.en: And now you don't need to put the answers to these in your bio, although you can, and you never really have to tell people the answers.
sentences.zh: 你不需要把这些答案写在简介里，当然写了也行，而且你其实永远不用直接告诉别人这些答案。

sentences.en: You simply have to write content and create products that help others change.
sentences.zh: 你只需要去写内容、去创造产品，帮别人发生改变就行了。

sentences.en: You have to create content on what you deem an important idea that helps people that align with those three questions we just asked.
sentences.zh: 你得围绕你认为重要的想法去创作内容，去帮助那些跟我们刚才三个问题对得上的人。

sentences.en: And now, if you struggle to answer even the first question there, I think a very good starting point for a lot of people in terms of who you can help the most is your past self.
sentences.zh: 如果你连第一个问题都很难回答，我觉得对很多人来说，一个非常好的起点——关于你能帮到最多的人是谁——就是过去的自己。

sentences.en: The person you can help the most is your past self, and there are plenty of other people who are like your past self.
sentences.zh: 你能帮到最多的人，就是过去的你，而且有大量的人跟过去的你很像。

sentences.en: You are pursuing your best self.
sentences.zh: 你在追求成为最好的自己。

sentences.en: So you're trying to get here, but you're here now and you were here before.
sentences.zh: 你想达到这个位置，但你此刻在这里，而之前你在那里。

sentences.en: There are plenty of people here.
sentences.zh: 有大量的人还在那里。

sentences.en: Those are who you can help.
sentences.zh: 那些人就是你能帮到的。

sentences.en: You don't need to posture as your best self, because a lot of the time that doesn't relate to the person down here.
sentences.zh: 你不需要摆出"最好的自己"的姿态，因为很多时候，那个姿态跟下面这里的人是没有共鸣的。

sentences.en: Usually if you're one to 2 to 3 steps ahead, that's what you want.
sentences.zh: 通常你领先一到两步、两到三步，那才是你想要的。

sentences.en: If I go to someone and say, hey, you want to make 5 million bucks and it's just average person, they're gonna be like, you're dumb.
sentences.zh: 如果我走到一个人面前说，嘿，你想赚500万美元吗，对方只是个普通人，他会觉得，你有病吧。

sentences.en: Like, why would I even believe you like that?
sentences.zh: 我凭什么要信你这种话？

sentences.en: Sounds like a scam.
sentences.zh: 听着就像骗局。

sentences.en: But if I came to you and say, hey, I learned this thing for how to make $100 a day.
sentences.zh: 但如果我走到你面前说，嘿，我学到一个方法，一天能赚100美元。

sentences.en: Do you want me to teach it to you?
sentences.zh: 你想让我教你吗？

sentences.en: There's least a bit more open, right?
sentences.zh: 至少会稍微更愿意听一下，对吧？

sentences.en: That's only one example.
sentences.zh: 这只是一个例子。

sentences.en: Like money related, that could still set off people's alarms, but I think you get the point.
sentences.zh: 跟钱相关的例子，还是可能触发别人的警觉，但我觉得你明白我的意思。

sentences.en: It's a lot closer in proximity to where they are and what they believe is possible for themselves to achieve.
sentences.zh: 这个目标离他们所在的位置更近，也更接近他们相信自己能做到的事。

sentences.en: So the questions that you ask yourself here are what situation were you in?
sentences.zh: 所以你要问自己的问题是：你当时处在什么处境？

sentences.en: How did you get into the interest that helped you change, and how can you help people go through the same transformation faster?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么接触到那个帮你改变的兴趣的，你又怎么帮别人更快地经历同样的转变？

sentences.en: And you really don't need to think too hard about this, because it will refine with time.
sentences.zh: 你真的不需要在这件事上想太多，因为它会随着时间慢慢变清晰的。

sentences.en: You just need like a starting point, you need a direction.
sentences.zh: 你只需要一个起点，一个方向。

sentences.en: So moving on to what your content is.
sentences.zh: 好，接下来聊聊你的内容是什么。

sentences.en: If your brand is the transformation, your content is the map that is built over time.
sentences.zh: 如果说你的品牌是那条蜕变之路，那你的内容就是随着时间慢慢铺开的地图。

sentences.en: It's the world.
sentences.zh: 它是整个世界。

sentences.en: You think of the Marvel Cinematic Universe with Iron Man and the Avengers and Spider-Man and all of these different things.
sentences.zh: 你想想漫威电影宇宙，有钢铁侠、复仇者联盟、蜘蛛侠，所有这些不同的东西。

sentences.en: It was built up over time in this like binge fashion, and they have TV show spinoffs, they have the movies, they have action figures, they have an entire lore behind it.
sentences.zh: 它是随着时间一点点搭建起来的，用一种让你追着看的方式，他们有电视剧衍生剧，有电影，有手办，背后还有一整套世界观。

sentences.en: That's kind of what you're building over time.
sentences.zh: 这差不多就是你在长期构建的东西。

sentences.en: And so for this, I talk to a lot of people who just want to start writing.
sentences.zh: 所以说到这个，我跟很多只想开始写作的人聊过。

sentences.en: And as you might guess, or as you may have experienced, their problems revolve around the same things.
sentences.zh: 你可能猜到了，或者你可能也经历过，他们的问题都绕不开那几件事。

sentences.en: They don't know what to write, and they don't know how to write it.
sentences.zh: 他们不知道写什么，也不知道怎么写。

sentences.en: They don't know what makes their writing different from everyone else's. They don't know why people would listen to them over someone else.
sentences.zh: 他们不知道自己的写作跟别人有什么不同，不知道为什么别人要听他们的，而不是听别人的。

sentences.en: They don't see themselves as experts but don't understand.
sentences.zh: 他们不觉得自己是专家，但他们没搞懂。

sentences.en: The experts aren't the only ones who have an audience.
sentences.zh: 不是只有专家才有受众。

sentences.en: You can build a student style personal brand to you.
sentences.zh: 你可以打造一个学生型的个人品牌。

sentences.en: Just learn, research, and share what you've found without claiming any results until you actually have results.
sentences.zh: 就是去学习、去研究、去分享你发现的东西，在你真正拿到结果之前，先别声称任何结果。

sentences.en: So I like to think of content like this.
sentences.zh: 所以我喜欢这样理解内容。

sentences.en: You have a brand who you help and how you help them change their life.
sentences.zh: 你有一个品牌，你帮谁、怎么帮他们改变人生。

sentences.en: And now you treat content like you're the programmer of a video game.
sentences.zh: 然后你把内容当成你在给一个电子游戏写程序。

sentences.en: You have point A, where your audience is now level one, and then you have point B where you can help them get to, which can be level 100 or 50 or ten or even two, just one level ahead of them.
sentences.zh: 你有 A 点，你的受众现在就在那里，一级；然后你有 B 点，你能帮他们到达的地方，可能是 100 级、50 级、10 级，甚至只是 2 级，就比他们领先一级。

sentences.en: And even if you aren't level 100, you're allowed to grow.
sentences.zh: 就算你不是 100 级，你也可以成长。

sentences.en: You should grow. Actually, you're the leader.
sentences.zh: 你应该成长。实际上，你是那个领路人。

sentences.en: That's why you attract followers, so to say, because entrepreneurship is self-improvement in disguise.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么你会吸引追随者，可以这么说，因为创业本质上就是伪装起来的自我提升。

sentences.en: Now, to make this simple, any idea or content is free game.
sentences.zh: 现在，为了让这件事简单一点，任何想法或内容都是自由可用的。

sentences.en: If it lands between your point A and point B, and it may help to quite literally pull out a piece of paper drop point A on one side, point B on the other, and then you can start filling in the middle with topics and ideas.
sentences.zh: 只要它落在你的 A 点和 B 点之间，你甚至可以真的拿出一张纸，一边写上 A 点，另一边写上 B 点，然后开始往中间填话题和想法。

sentences.en: So to start, you can write 2 to 3 broad topics like health, psychology or business.
sentences.zh: 所以一开始，你可以写 2 到 3 个宽泛的主题，比如健康、心理学或商业。

sentences.en: These are your content pillars or your main interests broadened up a bit.
sentences.zh: 这些就是你的内容支柱，或者说你的主要兴趣，稍微拓宽一点。

sentences.en: And then for each of those topics, you can write 2 to 3 more subtopics.
sentences.zh: 然后，针对每一个主题，你可以再写 2 到 3 个子主题。

sentences.en: For each of those subtopics, you can write 2 to 3 pain points, principles, how to's, or other types of content styles that you've seen.
sentences.zh: 针对每一个子主题，你可以写 2 到 3 个痛点、原则、操作指南，或者你见过的其他内容形式。

sentences.en: And so let's say that my brand is to help people become future proof, which it is.
sentences.zh: 假设我的品牌是帮人变得面向未来，事实也确实如此。

sentences.en: That's my niche, so to speak.
sentences.zh: 可以这么说，这就是我的细分领域。

sentences.en: That's who I try to attract, is people who want to become future proof.
sentences.zh: 我试图吸引的就是那些想变得面向未来的人。

sentences.en: Then my entire goal with content at that point is to find great ideas that I want to talk about, and just frame them through the lens of becoming future proof.
sentences.zh: 那么到了这一步，我做内容的全部目标就是找到我想聊的好想法，然后只是通过“变得面向未来”这个视角去框定它们。

sentences.en: So if I want to talk about the topics of having multiple interests, the way it becomes unique to me is like, okay, well, how does that help you become future proof in this video was born as an example.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我想聊“拥有多重兴趣”这个话题，它对我来说变得独特的方式就是：好，那这怎么帮你变得面向未来？这个视频就是这样诞生的，作为一个例子。

sentences.en: If I'm studying my interests like flow psychology and I find an idea I love like how psychic entropy causes the mind to slowly become disordered with time.
sentences.zh: 如果我在研究我感兴趣的东西，比如心流心理学，我找到一个我喜欢的观点，比如精神熵如何让心智随着时间慢慢变得失序。

sentences.en: Unless effort is put into maintaining a meaningful hierarchy of goals, then the first question I ask myself is this how does this apply to becoming future proof?
sentences.zh: 除非你刻意投入努力去维持一个有意义的层级化目标体系，那我问自己的第一个问题就是：这怎么应用到“变得面向未来”上？

sentences.en: And through that question alone, I now have a unique piece of content.
sentences.zh: 光是透过这个问题，我就产出了一段独一无二的内容。

sentences.en: I'm not copying the idea 1 to 1, I'm applying it to a new domain from my own voice and perspective.
sentences.zh: 我不是一比一照搬那个想法，而是用自己的声音和视角，把它应用到一个新的领域。

sentences.en: And that is content creation in a nutshell.
sentences.zh: 这就是内容创作的核心。

sentences.en: For people who don't want to dance in front of a camera or be on TikTok, just hunt for ideas in your interest that you really like, and you have a mission that you can help other people achieve.
sentences.zh: 对于那些不想在镜头前跳舞、也不想上 TikTok 的人来说，你只需要在你真正感兴趣的领域里寻找想法，并且你有一个使命，能帮别人达成某个目标。

sentences.en: And then you tie the two together.
sentences.zh: 然后把这两者绑在一起。

sentences.en: You frame the idea through the mission.
sentences.zh: 用你的使命去框定那个想法。

sentences.en: So when you have an idea, you just look at the map that you drew with all of your topics on there and you think, okay, how does this help people get from point A to point B? Okay.
sentences.zh: 所以当你有一个想法时，你就看看你画的那张包含所有主题的地图，然后想：好，这怎么帮人从 A 点走到 B 点？明白了吗？

sentences.en: In the newsletter YouTube video you're creating, the introduction is illustrating the problem that point A is at the middle is explaining the concept or idea that you want to talk about.
sentences.zh: 在你写的 newsletter 或 YouTube 视频里，开头是描绘 A 点所在的问题，中间是解释你想讲的概念或想法。

sentences.en: And then the end section or the actionable section is like, okay, here's the steps to get to point B, and that's how you create a newsletter.
sentences.zh: 然后结尾部分，也就是可操作的部分，就像是：好，这是到达 B 点的步骤。这就是你写 newsletter 的方式。

sentences.en: That's how you create a YouTube script.
sentences.zh: 这就是你写 YouTube 脚本的方式。

sentences.en: That's how you create anything long form for short form content, you kind of just idiot short posts.
sentences.zh: 这就是你创作任何长内容的方式。至于短内容，你基本上就是写一些短小精悍的帖子。

sentences.en: And it really helps to look at how other people package and structure posts.
sentences.zh: 而且，去看看别人怎么包装和结构化帖子，真的很有帮助。

sentences.en: If you don't know what to do here, this is when you go to Eden and look at how other posts are doing, and then click the buttons that allow you to make them your own.
sentences.zh: 如果你不知道这里该怎么做，这时候你就去 Eden 看看其他帖子是怎么做的，然后点那些按钮，把它们变成你自己的东西。

sentences.en: And that's a very important part, because if you can't get people to click and stay.
sentences.zh: 这是非常重要的一环，因为如果你没法让人点进来并留下来——

sentences.en: In other words, if you can't create engaging content from the ideas you have, who's going to see your product?
sentences.zh: 换句话说，如果你没法用你的想法创造出有吸引力的内容，谁会看到你的产品？

sentences.en: Who is going to pay you for what you do?
sentences.zh: 谁会为你做的事付钱？

sentences.en: In other words, how are you actually going to do what you love learning in a sustainable way?
sentences.zh: 再换句话说，你到底要怎么以一种可持续的方式，去做你热爱学习的事？

sentences.en: If you're always in survival mode and selling a product for your boss rather than yourself?
sentences.zh: 如果你一直处于生存模式，在为你的老板而不是为你自己卖产品？

sentences.en: So that moves us on to the product, right?
sentences.zh: 这就把我们带到了产品上，对吧？

sentences.en: Your brand is the transformation, your content is the map, and your product is the tool.
sentences.zh: 你的品牌是转变，你的内容是地图，你的产品是工具。

sentences.en: Now, when I first started on social media, I was a web designer.
sentences.zh: 我刚上社交媒体的时候，是个网页设计师。

sentences.en: I started writing on Twitter because I was tired of doing cold outreach all day.
sentences.zh: 我开始在 Twitter 上写作，是因为我厌倦了整天做冷推广。

sentences.en: It was frankly exhausting, and I knew that my next step was building an audience so that I could land clients from that audience.
sentences.zh: 坦白说那太累人了，而且我知道我的下一步是建立受众，这样我就能从受众里接到客户。

sentences.en: As I got clients.
sentences.zh: 随着我接到客户——

sentences.en: And as my service evolved because my knowledge evolved with it, I found a lot of people coming to me, not because they wanted a website, but because they just didn't have clarity on their brand, content, and product.
sentences.zh: 随着我的服务不断进化，因为我的知识也跟着进化——我发现很多人来找我，不是因为他们想要一个网站，而是因为他们对自己的品牌、内容和产品完全没有清晰的认知。

sentences.en: They thought a website was going to fix everything, or they were convinced that that was like the whole and why they weren't making money as a website of all things.
sentences.zh: 他们以为一个网站能解决一切，或者他们被说服了，觉得那就是全部，觉得他们赚不到钱的原因，竟然是网站这种东西。

sentences.en: When the rest of the things the brand content product like literally the main funnel that would make you money just wasn't there.
sentences.zh: 而其他那些东西——品牌、内容、产品，也就是真正能让你赚钱的主要漏斗——根本就不存在。

sentences.en: And so I helped them, and I actually started to pivot my offer in that direction.
sentences.zh: 所以我帮了他们，而且我实际上开始把我的服务往那个方向调整。

sentences.en: And there was a two year period of time where I would consider myself a brand advisor or personal brand advisor.
sentences.zh: 有两年时间，我会把自己看作一个品牌顾问，或者说个人品牌顾问。

sentences.en: And the biggest question then was, okay, if I write about all these ideas and interests, what do I sell?
sentences.zh: 那时候最大的问题是：好，如果我写所有这些想法和兴趣，那我卖什么？

sentences.en: It feels like I'm just giving everything out.
sentences.zh: 感觉我好像把什么都免费给出去了。

sentences.en: People won't have a reason to buy my product if they already know it all.
sentences.zh: 人们如果已经全都知道了，就不会有理由买我的产品了。

sentences.en: And now, typically the reason people ask this question is because they just love getting in their own heads, right?
sentences.zh: 通常，人们问这个问题的原因，就是因为他们太喜欢自己胡思乱想了，对吧？

sentences.en: They don't like thinking things through.
sentences.zh: 他们不喜欢把事情想透彻。

sentences.en: And I'm not saying that as a jab.
sentences.zh: 我这么说不是在嘲讽谁。

sentences.en: I do it all the time, right?
sentences.zh: 我自己也经常这样，对吧？

sentences.en: You get a little bit stressed, you don't know where to look.
sentences.zh: 你稍微有点压力，就不知道该往哪看。

sentences.en: And you just like pick an answer, right?
sentences.zh: 然后你就随便选了个答案，对吧？

sentences.en: And then that answer becomes law and then it prevents you from taking any further action.
sentences.zh: 然后那个答案就变成了铁律，阻止你采取任何进一步的行动。

sentences.en: And so that answer to that of like, oh, why will they buy from me is that people just buy things they probably don't remember everything they read from you, and they are even more likely to never implement it.
sentences.zh: 所以，对于"别人凭什么跟我买"这个问题，那个答案就是：人们就是会买东西，他们可能根本不记得你写过的所有内容，而且他们更有可能永远不会去执行。

sentences.en: Just because you've talked about it doesn't mean people aren't going to buy something.
sentences.zh: 你聊过某个话题，不代表人们就不会买相关的东西。

sentences.en: But of course, there's a better way to think about it, right?
sentences.zh: 但当然，有更好的思考方式，对吧？

sentences.en: That's kind of a silly way to think about it.
sentences.zh: 刚才那种想法其实挺蠢的。

sentences.en: I like to think of my products as tools or systems that help people get from point A to point B on my map.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢把我的产品看作工具或系统，帮助人们在我的地图上从A点走到B点。

sentences.en: As an example, I can talk about writing all day, and I can teach how I write newsletters, content and generate ideas.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，我可以整天聊写作，我可以教别人我怎么写newsletter、做内容和产生创意。

sentences.en: But a tweet or newsletter is usually not the best medium for teaching an entire system through things like modules, worksheets, templates, and everything like that.
sentences.zh: 但一条推文或一篇newsletter，通常不是教授一整套系统的最佳媒介，因为系统需要模块、练习册、模板之类的东西。

sentences.en: So if I create a product like I did previously with to our writer when I was actually promoting and selling that, that was like the complete system for implementation.
sentences.zh: 所以如果我做一个产品，就像我之前做的Two Hour Writer，在我真正推广和销售它的时候，那就是一套完整的执行系统。

sentences.en: Like no one video could take the role of that product because it was a daily set of actions backed with education that someone can use to get results.
sentences.zh: 没有任何一个单独的视频能替代那个产品，因为它是一套每日行动方案，背后有教育支撑，能让人真正拿到结果。

sentences.en: And it's kind of evolved into what Eden is becoming today.
sentences.zh: 它后来也慢慢演变成了今天Eden的样子。

sentences.en: It's find validated ideas.
sentences.zh: 找到经过验证的创意。

sentences.en: Make them your own, right?
sentences.zh: 把它们变成你自己的，对吧？

sentences.en: Post them.
sentences.zh: 发出去。

sentences.en: It's the writing hub, it's the content strategy hub.
sentences.zh: 这就是写作中心，这就是内容策略中心。

sentences.en: And one thing we need to talk about is that if you don't care to sell an info product because everyone told you they were a scam and you were dumb enough to not think or question, then you can build a software.
sentences.zh: 还有一件事我们必须聊聊：如果你不在乎卖信息产品，因为所有人都告诉你那是骗局，而你也蠢到不去思考或质疑，那你也可以做软件。

sentences.en: But again, and I've learned this through three years of failure so far, it needs to be a system.
sentences.zh: 但话说回来，我花了三年失败才学到这一点：它必须是一个系统。

sentences.en: Yes, you can probably vibe code small scale software quite well if you have agency and understand the iterative process and you love learning, so you should be able to just start building it and ask the AI questions along the way.
sentences.zh: 是的，如果你有自主性，理解迭代过程，并且热爱学习，你大概可以用vibe coding的方式把小型软件做得相当好，所以你应该能直接开始构建，然后一路向AI提问。

sentences.en: And the thing here that I don't get is like, oh, well, how do I start?
sentences.zh: 而这里我不理解的是，总有人说"呃，那我怎么开始？"

sentences.en: Just ask Claude, how do I start building an app?
sentences.zh: 直接问Claude：我怎么开始构建一个应用？

sentences.en: Literally just say that, hey, I want to build it.
sentences.zh: 就原话这么说：嘿，我想构建一个应用。

sentences.en: I've heard about this vibe coding thing.
sentences.zh: 我听说了这个叫vibe coding的东西。

sentences.en: I've heard that you can help with this.
sentences.zh: 我听说你能帮我做这个。

sentences.en: How do I do it?
sentences.zh: 我该怎么做？

sentences.en: Give me a plan and then it breaks it.
sentences.zh: 给我一个计划，然后它就会把计划拆解出来。

sentences.en: Down you go.
sentences.zh: 然后你就去做。

sentences.en: Okay, how do I start on step one?
sentences.zh: 好，第一步怎么开始？

sentences.en: And then it tells you and then you do it and you go, okay, let's do step two.
sentences.zh: 然后它告诉你，你就去做，做完你说，好，我们做第二步。

sentences.en: And then you tell and you do it.
sentences.zh: 然后你告诉它，你再去做。

sentences.en: And it's not like you're just having Claude do everything because you have to guide it.
sentences.zh: 而且这不像你让Claude包办一切，因为你得引导它。

sentences.en: You still have to understand what's going on.
sentences.zh: 你还是得理解到底在发生什么。

sentences.en: And then you keep just following the steps until you have a version one.
sentences.zh: 然后你就一直跟着步骤走，直到做出一个初版。

sentences.en: And frankly, the version one is going to suck.
sentences.zh: 坦白说，初版一定会很烂。

sentences.en: And then it's up to you.
sentences.zh: 接下来就看你了。

sentences.en: Are you going to say, oh yeah, this is a vibe coded app.
sentences.zh: 你是会说，哦对，这是个 vibe coded 应用。

sentences.en: So I could only get this far and it sucks.
sentences.zh: 所以我也就只能做到这儿了，它很烂。

sentences.en: Or are you going to keep going, keep iterating, and you just ask the question or solve the problem when you encounter it?
sentences.zh: 还是说你会继续推进、持续迭代，遇到问题就去问、就去解决？

sentences.en: Now back to the point.
sentences.zh: 现在回到正题。

sentences.en: The creator economy when it comes to monetization is a systems economy.
sentences.zh: 创作者经济，在变现这件事上，本质上是一个系统经济。

sentences.en: You don't have to build the next note taking tool.
sentences.zh: 你不需要去造下一个笔记工具。

sentences.en: I've tried that you build the software that helps them do what your info product would have helped them do.
sentences.zh: 我试过，你打造软件，帮他们做到你的信息产品本来要帮他们做到的事。

sentences.en: Watch my previous videos on the info product or go to my Substack and on my page.
sentences.zh: 去看我之前关于信息产品的视频，或者去我的 Substack 和我的页面。

sentences.en: Here I have a full guide to how you would create a profitable digital product that gives you everything that's like what you need to know about marketing.
sentences.zh: 这里我有一份完整指南，教你如何打造一个能盈利的数字产品，里面包含了所有你需要知道的营销知识。

sentences.en: You don't need to take any other marketing course except for pay attention to what's in that guide.
sentences.zh: 你不需要再上任何其他营销课程，只需要认真看那份指南里的内容。

sentences.en: So for Paul Mousseau, who has the philosophy school that we talked about earlier, he could literally just build like a learning app for philosophy and he could share his teachings on there.
sentences.zh: 所以拿 Paul Mousseau 来说，他开了我们之前聊到的那所哲学学校，他完全可以就做一个哲学学习应用，在上面分享他的教学内容。

sentences.en: Like, there are so many different ideas that could work for Paul, but I'm sure Paul doesn't care because he's already doing something that works well.
sentences.zh: 真的，有太多不同的想法对 Paul 都可行，但我确定 Paul 不在乎，因为他已经在做一件运转得很好的事了。

sentences.en: He doesn't need to go further.
sentences.zh: 他不需要再往前走了。

sentences.en: I'm just kind of throwing out ideas here and there, but that's really it.
sentences.zh: 我只是随便抛出一些想法，但真的就是这样。

sentences.en: You just have to build the product and you have to do it in a way that gets results or is good.
sentences.zh: 你只需要把产品做出来，而且你得用一种能出结果、或者说够好的方式去做。

sentences.en: You can have this great idea and you can build it out, but that doesn't mean it's good and it doesn't mean that other people want to use it.
sentences.zh: 你可以有一个很棒的想法，也可以把它做出来，但这不代表它就好，也不代表别人就想用。

sentences.en: And it definitely doesn't mean that they want to pay for it.
sentences.zh: 更不代表他们愿意为它付钱。

sentences.en: So you have to test all of those things.
sentences.zh: 所以这些你都得去测试。

sentences.en: And so with all of that, this wasn't a very hyper practical video or section on building a product, because I don't think that's what you need.
sentences.zh: 所以综合以上，这一部分并不是一个特别实操的、关于如何打造产品的视频或章节，因为我觉得你需要的不是这个。

sentences.en: You just need clarity that this path is viable.
sentences.zh: 你只需要一个清晰的认知：这条路是可行的。

sentences.en: That's why you came to this video.
sentences.zh: 这才是你来看这个视频的原因。

sentences.en: It's not for the step by step how to do it, because you can find that anywhere.
sentences.zh: 不是为了手把手的操作步骤，因为那个你在哪儿都能找到。

sentences.en: You just need the belief.
sentences.zh: 你只是需要那个信念。

sentences.en: And once you have that belief, you can figure out the rest because you love learning.
sentences.zh: 一旦你有了那个信念，剩下的你都能自己搞定，因为你热爱学习。

sentences.en: So this video was just meant to be a spark to show you what's possible.
sentences.zh: 所以这个视频只是想成为一个火花，让你看到什么是可能的。

sentences.en: And I'll create more on this in the future.
sentences.zh: 未来我会做更多相关内容。

sentences.en: Or just let me know what you actually want to learn, and I'll jot that down to create another video about it.
sentences.zh: 或者直接告诉我你到底想学什么，我会记下来，再做一个视频。

sentences.en: But until then, like subscribe, join my newsletter link in the description if you want weekly newsletters on how to reach your potential.
sentences.zh: 但在此之前，点赞、订阅、加入我的 newsletter，链接在简介里，如果你想每周收到关于如何发挥潜能的 newsletter。

sentences.en: And then check out Eden.
sentences.zh: 然后去看看 Eden。

sentences.en: If you're even slightly interested in finding high performing ideas that relate exactly to you and having them delivered to you on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 如果你哪怕有一点点兴趣，想找到与你高度相关的高价值想法，并且每天都能收到它们。

sentences.en: So with that, thank you for watching.
sentences.zh: 好了，感谢观看。

sentences.en: I'll see you in the next video. Bye.
sentences.zh: 下个视频见。拜。
